races.name: Coral Goodwood Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Maxi King
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in this race; Kevin Philippart De Foy's gelding is ideally suited by uncontested lead conditions on Good to Firm, won here at Goodwood over 2m2f last time, and Toby Moore's 7lb claim helps offset a competitive OR=103 — the key question is whether he is caught late up the hill.
runners_data.comment: Maxi King has been knocking on the door, a second two starts back and a third four starts back highlighting consistent placed efforts, and he has experience of today's going — the concern is that he remains yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over for Michael Bell and this horse has strong course form at Goodwood, though his last two runs here were unplaced; his style fits prominent racing and he is likely to push forward from his high draw, but his recent form string (1-1576) shows declining returns.
runners_data.comment: Duke of Oxford won two of his last five starts and returns on a quick 20-day turnaround in good heart, with experience of today's going working in his favour. Carrying 137 lb is the one ask, but his recent winning form makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Defiantly
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old wore a hood last time and has twice placed at Goodwood over staying distances; this trip looks within range, but a wide draw and 45 days off slightly temper expectations for Dylan Browne McMonagle who will need a clean passage in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Defiantly has run over today's trip and going before, and he comes here fresh after 45 days off carrying 133 lb — second last time out is the standout angle. The main risk is he's winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Valiancy
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old carries a hood and has a striking Goodwood record (three wins including a course-and-distance victory), has handled Good to Firm well (8 from 8 going-compatible runs), and James Doyle can ensure he travels prominently — this is one of the standout course profiles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Valiancy boasts back-to-back wins in his recent form and has experience of today's going, making him a serious threat off 132 lb; the main concern is whether a 45-day absence has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Andrew Balding six-year-old who won twice over 2m at Sandown and has a positive record on quicker ground; his last two Goodwood runs were disappointing but those were over shorter distances — this trip extension is a live key.
runners_data.comment: Berkshire Sundance won two of his last five starts, with those victories three and four runs back, but eighth last time out suggests he's struggling to recapture that form; he has going experience to call on, though 131 lb is a stiff burden.

runners_data.name: Annabel's Ghost
runners_data.note: French raider from M Seror's yard, ridden by Pierre-Charles Boudot, who holds a single going-compatible run and was fifth on her reappearance here at Goodwood over 2m; a genuine hold-up runner whose chance depends on the pace being strong enough from the front.
runners_data.comment: Annabel's Ghost has experience over today's trip and rates 4 lb above his official mark, but a fifth last time out and a stable firing at just 3% in the last 14 days are real concerns; his sole win comes five starts back, with a third four starts back the only other encouragement in recent runs.

runners_data.name: Alphonse Le Grande
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for A J Martin and Jamie Powell placed in his trainer's most recent runner; his going-compatible form is modest (9 from 15, one win) and recent form figures of 87-005 do not inspire confidence, making this a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Alphonse Le Grande at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a rating of 92 suggests some unexploited ability — though recent finishes make it hard to fancy him strongly against a field of 18.

runners_data.name: Believitanducan
runners_data.note: William Buick partners a horse that has won three of his last four starts (all at Sandown over 2m), going well under Good to Firm conditions, and his strike rate is compelling — he has never run at Goodwood before, which is the only query against an otherwise strong profile.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Believitanducan rates an outsider on these terms despite a striking run of three wins in his last four starts; he has experience of today's going, but the ratings gap is hard to overcome.

runners_data.name: Anniversary
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old runs in a hood and has been consistently placed over staying trips at Goodwood with a second over course and distance; a hold-up runner in Jamie Spencer's hands who needs a true pace to deliver, and his record of 555275 shows he knocks on the door without winning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; Anniversary has going experience in his favour and returns after 20 days, but the recent record of fifths and a seventh underlines the task he faces here.

runners_data.name: Charging Thunder
runners_data.note: James Owen's eight-year-old, lightly turned around after just 12 days, won at Goodwood over 2m2f last month and handles the track and conditions well; David Probert has the course knowledge and this horse's stamina is proven — the short turnaround bears monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some hope, and his trainer is in fine shape at 35% over the past fortnight; he has run over today's going before, but an unplaced effort 12 days ago leaves something to prove.

runners_data.name: Highwind
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' six-year-old travels from Ireland and wears a hood; four runs at Goodwood all produced placed efforts around 4th-8th and he handles the track, but Good to Firm going has been his standard environment and his hold-up style is dependent on genuine tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Highwind does at least bring going experience to the table and a our rating fractionally above his official mark suggests some residual ability — yet a sixth and eighth punctuate that sequence, making him a hard one to fancy from mid-table.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's consistent placer has three straight third-place finishes in similar staying handicaps; by nature a front-runner, he has been placed in midfield on the map as there are simply too many prominent types for all to secure their desired position — his chance is conditioned by whether he can get forward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sax Appeal has nonetheless shown consistent placing ability, landing four thirds in recent starts; he has run over today's going before, yet ranked 12 of 18 on our ratings, he faces a stiff ask from 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Kings
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old ran twice in France placing both times over staying distances, and has since placed twice in British handicaps; he wants to race prominently but the density of the prominent group means he will likely be shuffled back, working against his natural game.
runners_data.comment: Consistent runner who has finished second three times in his last five starts, though winless in that spell and a 70-day break needs to be factored in; has experience of today's going and the 87 rating suggests he holds his own in this field.

runners_data.name: St Mawes
runners_data.note: George Scott's four-year-old has won twice and placed twice from five attempts at Goodwood, giving him the best course profile in the field on raw numbers; instinctively a prominent racer, he will be squeezed for position in this large field and raced here last just 14 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, St Mawes faces a stiff ask, and a void run complicates his recent profile; he was a winner four and five starts back, and second two starts back shows some form, while he has experience of today's going and is fit enough at 14 days since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Kentucky River
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's four-year-old with a strong staying pedigree (won over 2m3f at Goodwood), ridden by the 3lb claimer Jack Nicholls; his hold-up style requires a strong gallop and his 58-day absence from racing is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Kentucky River arrives 58 days between runs and ranks 17th of 18 on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite winning last time out; he has experience of today's going, but the weight of evidence points elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Aggagio
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield due to redistribution pressure; his recent form of 34-536 is modest and while he has placed over staying trips on softer ground, Good to Firm at Goodwood on a long trip asks questions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third two runs back his best recent effort, Aggagio has run over today's trip and going before but a ranking of 13th of 18 on our figures makes it hard to build a case for him here.

runners_data.name: Gooloogong
runners_data.note: George Baker's six-year-old won this type of race at Sandown but has since finished sixth at Sandown, and placed in midfield mostly at Flat tracks; a prominent runner by inclination who cannot get that position here given the traffic, which substantially reduces his chance.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive finishes of sixth and fourth in his last two starts make Gooloogong hard to fancy despite a win three starts back, and he ranks 16th of 18 on our figures; today's going holds no fears on past experience, but he has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old runs just seven days after his last start and has a mixed Goodwood record; a prominent type by nature, Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim is a positive, but racing out of her natural position in a field this congested at this trip is a real handicap.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Trojan Sun arrives unplaced last time out and sixth three starts back, with his sole recent victory coming four starts back; going experience helps, but he faces a stiff ask from this position in the rankings.

races.paceDynamic: Maxi King is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field over 2m4½f on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, and with no genuine rival willing to take him on early, he is almost certain to control the pace from the off — likely at a measured, energy-conserving gallop that suits his profile perfectly. The race is further congested by an unusually high volume of prominent-running types: Sax Appeal, Sea Of Kings, St Mawes, Gooloogong, Trojan Sun, Defiantly, Duke Of Oxford, Valiancy, Berkshire Sundance, Believitanducan, and Alphonse Le Grande all have prominent tendencies, meaning the field holds far more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — of these, Duke Of Oxford, Valiancy, Berkshire Sundance, Believitanducan, and Defiantly are the most likely to actually secure positions immediately behind Maxi King given their ratings, jockey quality, and recent course form. A sustainable, tempo-controlled race over this marathon trip on quick ground — with a lone leader setting an honest but uncontested gallop — typically resolves in favour of horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final climb at Goodwood's unique finishing straight, rather than pure closers who need genuine end-to-end pace to generate momentum from the rear. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers with stamina and course form, and penalises hold-up horses who will be dependent on Maxi King setting a hot enough pace to bring them into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maxi King Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Maxi King dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field fails to close him down through the Goodwood straight.
scenarios.body: Maxi King settles in front without any pressure, conserves energy through the long trip, and only needs to repel the closers in the final half-mile; at OR=103 on Good to Firm at Goodwood, he has the class and conditions to see it out. Prominent horses who travel smoothly behind him — particularly Valiancy and Berkshire Sundance — are best positioned to reel him in if he tires, making this a race between the front and the immediately prominent group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Finishers Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Maxi King's gallop is just strong enough to stretch the hold-up horses but not strong enough to sustain his own effort to the line.
scenarios.body: The prominent group behind Maxi King — Valiancy, Berkshire Sundance, and Believitanducan — travel comfortably within themselves before asserting in the final two furlongs as Maxi King's advantage is eroded by the uphill finish. Valiancy's strong Goodwood course form (three wins at the track) and Believitanducan's hat-trick of wins entering this race make them the most dangerous finishers in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Exploit Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely crawling in the early stages, causing bunching and allowing the hold-up horses to travel with minimal effort before the race ignites late.
scenarios.body: A false gallop over this trip can paradoxically compress the field and allow horses like Charging Thunder, Annabel's Ghost, and Anniversary to arrive late with energy saved; Charging Thunder won over course and distance at Goodwood and has the stamina profile to capitalise on a sprint-home scenario. However, this shape is dependent on Maxi King failing to control fractions effectively, which looks unlikely given his front-running profile and the distance of the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pack Overwhelms Leader
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types push forward aggressively early, forcing Maxi King into a faster pace and setting up a wide-open finish.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of prominent-running horses in this field creates a small but real risk that jockeys like Ryan Moore (Duke Of Oxford) or Oisin Murphy (Berkshire Sundance) push forward and inadvertently quicken the pace, turning the race into a test of raw stamina that benefits hold-up horses with proven staying ability. In this shape, Sea Of Kings' consistent placed form over staying trips and St Mawes' class could emerge late, though their redistribution to midfield means they are racing out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Valiancy (James Doyle) is the horse to watch tracking Maxi King — three Goodwood wins including over course and distance, proven on Good to Firm, and William Haggas in excellent form; if he travels smoothly in the prominent group he is the most dangerous challenger to the leader.

Believitanducan (William Buick) has won three of his last four starts and carries strong form into this, though his Goodwood debut is the one unknown — watch whether Buick deploys him prominently as expected given his natural style.

The sheer volume of prominent-running types (Sax Appeal, Sea Of Kings, St Mawes, Gooloogong, Trojan Sun) all jostling for the same positions early in an 18-runner field creates significant collision risk and potential pace disruption in the first mile — watch for erratic early sectionals.

Charging Thunder (David Probert) returns just 12 days after winning at Goodwood over course and distance — watch whether the quick turnaround leaves him flat or whether James Owen has deliberately targeted this race off the back of that win.

St Mawes holds the most concentrated Goodwood course form in the field (2W3P from 5 runs), but his redistribution to midfield due to pace crowding means he must overcome a tactical disadvantage — monitor his early position to see if Ray Dawson pushes him forward regardless.

races.name: HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's lightly-raced three-year-old has placed twice at Goodwood including this trip, but he is a natural pace-prominent runner who this map has shifted to midfield given the overcrowding up front; his 41-day absence and a form string ending in a seventh here last time temper enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Andab has been consistently thereabouts, placing second and third in four of his last five starts before a seventh last time out, and he has run over today's trip. The concern is that 41 days off the track may have left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Catullus
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's colt won nicely over 7f at Goodwood last time and rates a genuine contender on OR 107, but he is a pace-prominent type pushed back into midfield by the volume of similar horses — his most recent run here was a ten-length tenth, and Billy Loughnane must compensate for a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning ways two starts back, but unplaced last time out casts doubt on his consistency; he has run over today's trip and carries 129 lb from stall five, while a speed rating of 94 suggests he may need to find more against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Five Ways
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner shows a modest recent form string of 4-7504, hasn't won beyond 6f in his history, and faces a stiff test stepping up in class at this trip on Good To Firm; naturally a pace-prominent horse, he cannot get that ground in this field and is racing a full furlong further than his winning distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Five Ways faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 20-day break from stall one, but the modest recent form — two fourths the best of it — makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas's progressive three-year-old has won three of his last four including two at Goodwood on fast ground, making him the most interesting challenger to the favourite; Tom Marquand can slot in behind Talk Of New York on the pace and his form profile reads as genuinely improving at this trip and going.
runners_data.comment: Saber Strike arrives here third last time out, and a winner three starts back, with his official mark of 107 underlining his class; the sixth two starts back is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Shayem
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's colt won over this exact course and distance last time at Goodwood, giving him a strong positional and form argument, and Clifford Lee knows this straight mile well; his last run was just 22 days ago, he handles the ground, and he rates the most likely beneficiary if Talk Of New York is even slightly below his best.
runners_data.comment: Shayem arrives here in fine nick — a winner last time out and second two starts back, with experience over today's trip and a fit 22-day turnaround; the main risk is whether 129 lb blunts his late effort.

runners_data.name: Talk Of New York
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner with OR 116, three wins at Goodwood in his last five including over this mile, and William Buick in the saddle — he is wearing a hood and has every ingredient to dominate this race shape from the front on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Talk Of New York has been in fine nick, winning three of his last five starts with a win two starts back, and returns from a 45-day break having run over today's trip before; third last time out shouldn't alarm, and at 129 lb he carries plenty but remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Yazin
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners the John & Thady Gosden-trained three-year-old who showed smart form winning back-to-back before a disappointing eighth at Goodwood last time; he is a naturally prominent-going type who this map has pushed to the rear, and 64 days off the track alongside that poor Goodwood run introduce real uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Yazin has won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and has run over today's trip, but that distant eighth last time out is a concern after 64 days off, and our rating ranks him last of the seven runners here.

races.paceDynamic: Talk Of New York is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival looking to press him hard from the gates, William Buick can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood's straight mile. The redistribution in this map matters: Catullus, Five Ways, and Andab are all natural prominent types who cannot all claim that ground, meaning at least two of them will be shuffled back from their preferred position and racing off an unfamiliar foot. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Talk Of New York is best-placed to secure the lead, with Saber Strike and Shayem the likeliest to claim the positions directly behind him. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can sit on or just behind a controlled pace and quicken off it, giving a significant edge to genuine on-pace travellers who do not need to be dropped out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Talk Of New York Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Talk Of New York leads at a measured pace and kicks clear entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Buick dictates on his own terms, the field strings out behind a steady-to-fair gallop, and the line comes too soon for those forced wide or back; Talk Of New York's OR 116 and strong Goodwood form make him the dominant force in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Talk Of New York sets an unusually slow pace and the race detonates late with a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the first half mile compresses the field and negates the front-runner's advantage, giving the horses pushed back from their natural prominent position a chance to motor through; Yazin, operating from the rear despite being a prominent type, could benefit if the race turns truly tactical.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Talk Of New York is pressed into a stronger gallop by Saber Strike or Catullus forcing the pace from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop on fast ground suits a high cruising speed rather than a late kick, rewarding horses with proven stamina at this trip and strong Goodwood records; Saber Strike's progressive form and two wins at Goodwood on similar ground make him a credible finisher in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early, disrupting each other's rhythm and creating a messy, stop-start race.
scenarios.body: Horses forced away from their natural running position struggle to settle, and the winner could emerge from an unexpected position mid-pack; Shayem, who has genuine Goodwood winning form and a flexible style, is best insulated against the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch Talk Of New York's early sections — if Buick elects to dawdle through the first two furlongs, the compressed field will turn this into a sprint finish that negates his ability to kick clear.

Monitor Catullus and Five Ways at the break — both are prominent types who cannot get their preferred position, and any scrimmaging in the first two furlongs could cost them ground they cannot recover on a tight straight-mile finish.

Yazin's 64-day absence is notable given his disappointing Goodwood run last time; if he fails to travel with his usual fluency in the early stages, Ryan Moore will have very little track left to mount a challenge.

Saber Strike's two Goodwood wins on comparable ground are a significant positive angle — watch whether Tom Marquand is able to slot him in the second position on the heels of Talk Of New York, as that would place him in the optimal spot for this race shape.

races.name: Coral Golden Mile (Class 2 Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has run seven of her last eight races at Goodwood and handles fast ground well (13/15 sim-going), but OR 105 and a prominent style flag suggests she may be used more conservatively than her lead tag implies; the STYLE_FIT of 0.91 tempers confidence in her front-end role holding firm throughout.
runners_data.comment: Cerulean Bay has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 110 ranks him second of 22 runners — a strong case for him being the chief danger here. A second four starts back shows he can threaten at this level, though he remains winless in recent starts and the quick five-day turnaround is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Archivist
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good-to-firm ground and boasts a 3W6P record in similar conditions; prominent style suits the expected race shape well, and the 44-day freshener for trainer Al Jehani (0/11 in 14 days) is worth noting as form may need to build.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but unplaced last time out, and 44 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; has experience of today's distance and going, though carrying 138 lb from stall 20 is no light task.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with three course wins and excellent Goodwood track record, handles fast ground well (10/15), and Muir & Grassick are 2/12 in the last 14 days; the drop from his peak efforts is manageable at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ebt's Guard nonetheless brings a consistent profile to the table — third last time out, with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 110 puts him top of this 22-runner field from stall 3 carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a horse that has won twice at Goodwood over the straight mile on good-to-firm; the 44-day break is a slight unknown but Balding (8/40 in 14 days) keeps horses fit and his form figures here are strong.
runners_data.comment: Mister Winston has winning form in recent starts — a winner two starts back and a winner four starts back — but came home unplaced last time out after 44 days off, so he returns here on a fitness query; he has experience of today's trip and going, though his 136 lb burden from stall 19 is no help.

runners_data.name: English Oak
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with two wins over this course and distance in his last five starts and 13/15 sim-going; Bughanaim's mount needs the race to develop from off the pace and benefits most if the tempo turns slow and the race becomes a sprint.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to finish second last time out after an unplaced run, and English Oak has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but 135 lb from stall 22 makes life harder for a horse ranked mid-division.

runners_data.name: Indalo
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance 27 days ago and has a 2W6P record in similar conditions; Roger Varian (8/21 in 14 days) is in strong form and a horse happy to race prominently off a genuine pace is ideally placed.
runners_data.comment: Indalo won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he carries 135 lb from stall 6 and ranks eighth of 22 on our ratings — enough ability to feature, though the weight is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Two Tempting
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a consistent 1W2P record on similar going but all five recent runs are on Sandown's all-weather, making the turf switch on fast ground at Goodwood after a 146-day layoff a meaningful concern.
runners_data.comment: Two Tempting shows consistent placing form — third last time out, and a winner five starts back — but 146 days off the track is a concern, and 133 lb is a stiff enough burden; he has run over today's distance and going, at least.

runners_data.name: Classic
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins at Goodwood over the mile and solid sim-going numbers (12/15); Hannon (11/52 in 14 days) is firing and the horse has the course craft to be dangerous, though recent form figures of 8-2-1-9-8 are patchy.
runners_data.comment: Classic showed a useful turn of form with a win three starts back, but his two most recent efforts — eighth and ninth — make it hard to trust him here, especially shouldering 132 lb from stall 12. He has run over today's trip and going, which at least ticks the experience box.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has failed to win in any of his last 13 outings on similar going (1W1P) and has finished eighth or worse in three of his last four; no obvious reason to believe the form reverses here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ozat nonetheless has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 106 suggests he retains ability; the concern is a consistent lack of placing, making it hard to fancy him strongly from stall five off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Scoville
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in all six starts on similar going (6/6, 2W2P) and trained by the in-form Haggas (7/38 in 14 days); a hold-up type who carries headgear (t) and needs the race to come to him, but his speed figures are sharp if a sprint finish develops.
runners_data.comment: Scoville showed he knows how to win when landing the spoils five starts back, and experience over today's trip and going underlines his claims — but back-to-back sevenths and eighths in recent starts are the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Blue Brother
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who won over this trip on soft going and placed twice from good ground, but pushed back to a midfield mapping because the field is saturated with pace-style horses; his actual chance depends on finding a slot near the front that the race shape may not offer.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Blue Brother nevertheless shaped with promise on his most recent outing and a rating of 107 from our assessors suggests he's ahead of his official mark — with today's trip already under his belt, he looks a serious threat, though that 43-day absence is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Godwinson
runners_data.note: Prominent style but deeply out of form (500-00 in last five at Goodwood) with a 0W0P record in 15 recent similar-going starts; difficult to make a case for improvement at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall 14, Godwinson faces an uphill task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 104 offers a sliver of encouragement; 44 days between runs leaves his sharpness open to question.

runners_data.name: Cosi Bello
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood over 7f and placed twice from similar going, but this horse's natural front-running instinct will be stifled by the field's depth — the pace saturation means she is unlikely to find her preferred berth, which significantly undermines her profile.
runners_data.comment: Cosi Bello won three starts back but has disappointed since, finishing unplaced and then sixth in his last two; he has run over today's distance and going, yet 130 lb from stall nine makes life harder for a gelding who needs to rediscover that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fade-in-finish type, which is a significant concern in a Goodwood mile where the final two furlongs are relentless; though he has course and distance wins to his name, the redistribution away from prominent ground means his best racing style is compromised from the off.
runners_data.comment: Mirsky has finished ninth and seventh in his last two starts, with two unplaced efforts before that, making him hard to fancy ranked 17 of 22 on our figures; a win five starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and he has distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Bunyola Bay
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on the rise with two wins in her last four including over course and distance; Ryan Moore aboard for Hannon (11/52 in 14 days) is a major booking, and her ability to race prominently makes her well-suited to the expected race shape despite her youth and light weight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and his speed rating gives little encouragement, Bunyola Bay arrives on the back of an eighth last time out despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back; he has run over today's trip and returns after 33 days, but he faces a stiff task from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Beagle Bay

races.paceDynamic: Cerulean Bay is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, and with no natural challenger likely to push across and pressure her early, she can dictate a controlled, even gallop from the front. Behind her, a cluster of genuine prominent racers — Archivist, Ebt's Guard, Mister Winston, Indalo, Bunyola Bay and others — will compete for the limited front-rank positions, creating a bunched, competitive mid-group rather than an extended field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position; Archivist, Mister Winston, Indalo and Bunyola Bay are the likeliest to actually secure prominent berths given their course form and jockey quality, while Blue Brother, Cosi Bello, Mirsky, Beagle Bay, Tribal Chief and Walsingham will be pushed wider or deeper than their natural style dictates. With a sustainable Cerulean Bay-set tempo on fast ground over a flat Goodwood mile, this race shape strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to race prominently without wasting energy — prominent racers tracking the pace in the first three or four positions are best placed, as the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to reward pure hold-up closers off the final bend.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cerulean Bay Dictates, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay leads at a controlled pace and the principals pressing her in second to fourth sweep past inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Cerulean Bay sets an honest but unforced tempo and horses sitting a length or two behind her travelling sweetly have first run off the home turn, enabling those with tactical speed to pick her off without needing a deep stamina reserve. Prominent racers with strong course form on fast ground are the clear beneficiaries as the race is decided between those closest to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts, Late Surge Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay sets a genuinely slow early gallop and the race turns into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A crawl up front compresses the field and turns the race into a tactical 2f dash, wiping out any early advantage and opening the door for hold-up types to produce a finishing burst from midfield. On quick ground at Goodwood, horses with high cruising speed and a sharp turn of foot off a slow pace — rather than genuine stamina — come into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Builds, Front Two Hold
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay is joined or pressed by a prominent rival from the off, creating a more genuine gallop that puts a premium on stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace filters out the less resolute prominent types and rewards the horse who can sustain their effort through the last quarter-mile rather than producing a quick burst. Horses with clean profiles over the trip on similar ground, proven to see out the Goodwood mile strongly, benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off Rail, Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant traffic problems and several fancied prominent types are blocked, allowing a lightly-regarded runner to slip through late.
scenarios.body: With 22 runners, interference through the home straight is a genuine risk, and a horse that finds a clean passage from a midfield position at the right moment can capitalise on the scramble ahead. Horses with the ability to quicken through a gap, even if currently out of market calculations, can benefit from the resulting disorder.

watchPoints.text: Bunyola Bay carries Ryan Moore for the in-form Hannon yard and won over this course and distance last time — if she secures a prominent berth in the first four, she is the primary danger to the market leaders given her improving profile and the race shape playing to her strengths.

Cerulean Bay's pace-setting role is the structural key to the entire race — if she dwells at the start or is pushed wider by the 22-runner field, the controlled tempo collapses and the tactical picture changes entirely for every runner behind her.

With eight or more natural prominent types unable to get their preferred position, the first two furlongs could see significant jostling for the limited front-rank berths, particularly from Blue Brother, Cosi Bello and Beagle Bay — watch for interference and bumping early that could compromise runners throughout the field.

Scoville's unbeaten record in six starts on similar going combined with the Haggas-Marquand combination and headgear flag makes him a horse to monitor if the tempo drops and a sharp late kick becomes the deciding factor in the closing stages.

Mister Winston's Oisin Murphy booking on a horse with a proven Goodwood mile record on fast ground is a significant market pointer — if he travels smoothly in the first three or four, the combination of jockey class and course craft could prove decisive.

races.paceDynamic: Asfoora is the confirmed front-runner and will stride directly to the front from the off on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, setting a sustainable gallop that is unlikely to be aggressively contested from a single rival. However, this field is saturated with prominent-racing types — American Affair, Jakajaro, Rumstar, Lamborghini Bf, Spicy Marg and Time For Sandals all want to race close to the pace, meaning there will be genuine pressure on Asfoora's flanks even if no single horse actively tries to shoot past at the break. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position, and of those, American Affair, Jakajaro and Rumstar are most likely to actually get in Asfoora's slipstream given their Goodwood course form and recent conditions form; Brussels, Jm Jungle, Aspect Island and Argentine Tango are genuine prominent racers who will find themselves trapped deeper than ideal. The sustained, honest pace over five furlongs on fast ground with a cluttered prominent group creates a race shape that strongly favours horses who can race close to the speed without burning themselves out — specifically the horse who can sit second or third off Asfoora and pounce in the final furlong, rewarding pace-positive but not front-running profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Asfoora leads, prominent pouncers strike
scenarios.trigger: If Asfoora dictates a clean, uncontested lead and the runners immediately off her settle into rhythm rather than scrapping for position.
scenarios.body: Asfoora sets honest fractions on fast ground and the horses able to sit second or third row — American Affair, Jakajaro, Rumstar — have the tactical position to challenge inside the final furlong without having wasted energy fighting for space; Good to Firm Goodwood suits all three and their course-form is strong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace bunches, prominent glut causes scrimmage

scenarios.body: A truly hot early gallop set or pressured by unexpectedly forward runners would stretch the field quickly and turn this into a test of raw speed and class over the full five furlongs; Night Raider and Spicy Marg, who can absorb a searching tempo and finish through beaten horses, are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.body: Night Raider has won over this course and trip from off the pace but needs pace to genuinely collapse in front of him, which is possible if the prominent glut burns each other out; the compressed final-furlong finish on fast Goodwood ground is the only realistic window for a true closer.

watchPoints.text: Jakajaro and American Affair — if either secures a clean pitch just off Asfoora in the first furlong they are ideally positioned in the most likely race shape and represent the highest-probability winning profiles.

Asfoora — monitor whether she actually clears to a solo lead or whether Rumstar or American Affair immediately press her, as any early pressure on her flanks fundamentally changes the pace dynamic from sustainable to hot.

Brussels and Jm Jungle — both are genuine prominent types redistributed into midfield; if either forces their way forward from wider draws in the first two furlongs they could inject unexpected early pace and compromise the field ahead of them.

Night Raider — James Doyle will be waiting for daylight from the rear; only worth monitoring seriously if the prominent glut creates a bunched, fast-run race — in a clean, measured gallop set by Asfoora alone, the hold-up horse's task becomes significantly harder.

Time For Sandals — five consecutive defeats at Goodwood despite a prominent style and good going record is a material red flag; if he does find early position it may simply ensure the pace is hotter than expected before he fades.

races.paceDynamic: Jonquil is the confirmed front-runner here, set to lead from the gates over Goodwood's 1m1f trip on Good To Firm ground, and with no genuine rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, she should dictate a measured, controlled gallop rather than a pressured pace. Diego Ventura, Boiling Point, and Dividend are all prominent-style runners who will press forward behind Jonquil, but Crown Of Oaks — a true prominent type — has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the queue ahead of her is too long; Boiling Point and Diego Ventura are most likely to secure the berths immediately behind the leader. The hold-up horses Galen, Haatem, Naqeeb, and Haatem will settle at the rear and look for a sustained late run, but Ambiente Friendly, though mapped to midfield, is in truth another hold-up type who is unlikely to get any closer than her natural position. With Jonquil able to dictate an honest but uncontested pace, this race shape strongly favours horses with a prominent racing style who can track the leader through the race and pounce in the straight without burning energy fighting for position — the tactical verdict is that prominent racers travelling smoothly behind Jonquil are advantaged, while deep hold-up horses face a searching test of their finishing speed over a trip that does not maximise their late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jonquil Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Jonquil leads unchallenged and sets a fair-to-honest pace, the race develops as a procession for those tracking her.
scenarios.body: Jonquil controls the tempo from the front and the prominent horses in her slipstream travel sweetly into the straight, where the winner emerges from the lead pack with a clean run; the even pace rewards those who have conserved energy rather than chased the race from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out, the hold-up horses get a true test and pick off tiring rivals in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest gallop set by Jonquil causes the prominent horses to empty inside the final furlong, opening a corridor for the closers to come through; this scenario requires the pace to be faster than expected on Good To Firm ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners jostle for the early lead or Jonquil is crowded and the pace becomes stop-start and tactical, the race degenerates into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race bunches the field and produces a scramble in the straight where position and luck in running become decisive; horses with tactical speed and an experienced jockey to find daylight are best placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent racer hits the front early in the straight and simply grinds on relentlessly as the pace steadily lifts through the race.
scenarios.body: Good To Firm ground at Goodwood over 1m1f rewards a horse with stamina to add to their speed when set a proper test; a staying-prominent type who wears rivals down through the final two furlongs rather than quickening past them benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Galen's going record is a perfect 15/15 at Goodwood on similar ground — if he gets a clear run from the rear in the straight he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race on pure course-ground fit.

Crown Of Oaks is a genuine prominent type who may be forced to race in a traffic pocket behind a full queue of prominent horses — watch whether Tom Marquand elects to push her forward early or accepts the midfield position, as that choice shapes her chance entirely.

Ambiente Friendly's redistribution to midfield disguises that his true comfort zone is at the rear over much longer trips; if he finds himself in an awkward position mid-pack without a clear run, Billy Loughnane may struggle to get a meaningful result.

Jonquil's STYLE_FIT flag is worth monitoring in the early stages — if she fails to stride out freely or is crowded at the start, the absence of a natural lead horse could briefly destabilise the field and trigger the tactical scenario where Crown Of Oaks benefits most.

The going report consistently confirms Good To Firm for this 1m1f contest, meaning the ground is fast enough to stretch the field and favour horses with genuine stamina at the distance — any horse whose recent wins have come on slower surfaces should be treated cautiously.

runners_data.comment: Persian Spring won two starts back but has been unplaced since, and 41 days off raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, though his rating of 87 leaves him facing stiffer company from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Sky Secret
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's consistent juvenile has won at Goodwood at 5f and remains well-handicapped on that form; Jack Nicholls claims 3lb and the horse has shown enough early pace to secure a prominent position even in a crowded field.
runners_data.comment: Sky Secret won two starts back but has finished fifth on his most recent outing, and while he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround, 134 lb from stall 8 makes life harder for a horse ranked fifth of eighteen.

runners_data.name: Revels
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's winner over 7f at Goodwood may find this 6f on the sharp side of his trip; the horse's prominent style should see him land a forward pitch but jumping back in trip is the key question after a 43-day break.
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time out but a winner two starts back, Revels has distance and going experience to call on and his trainer is in fine nick; the 132 lb burden and draw 16 are the balancing factors here.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this Andrew Balding-trained juvenile who has course form at 5f and 6f; listed as unknown style, Murphy's tactical intelligence makes him a wildcard who could slot in wherever gaps appear.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out but fourth in each of the two starts before that, The Dancing Pirate is winless in his last three; he has run over today's trip and going, and 131 lb from stall two keeps him honest — our rating of 88 suggests he holds a little in hand.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Has course-and-distance form on Firm but his most recent Goodwood run was over 5f in just Good to Firm and he finished 11th, so his suitability to this surface and track is mixed; a step up to 6f gives him a chance to settle better from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Glory bounced back to win two starts back and was third three starts back, giving him a lively recent profile over today's trip; from stall 17 carrying 131 lb, the 41-day absence is the one query, but his rating of 102 marks him as the clear form pick.

runners_data.name: Jaijai
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race — Hannon's juvenile has four Goodwood starts and has already won here over 5f on Good to Firm; Pat Dobbs will likely take him straight to the front on the rail and control the pace, making him a significant tactical factor regardless of his finishing position.
runners_data.comment: Jaijai arrives here in excellent nick — a winner two starts back and placed last time out, returning after 18 days carrying 131 lb from stall 15. He has experience of both today's trip and going, and our rating of 90 makes him a clear threat; the weight he shoulders is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Clash Of Hearts
runners_data.note: Keatley's 2yo is admirably consistent with a win and two placings at Goodwood — all at the track, all on similar going; his prominent style is well-suited to the scenario here and M.P. Sheehy will look to slot in just behind Jaijai from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Clash Of Hearts brings solid recent form — a winner last time out, and placed in both starts before that — and has experience of today's distance and going. The main concern is whether 40 days between runs leaves him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking elevates this Ben Haslam-trained juvenile considerably; won his last start at 5f on soft ground so the Good to Firm trip-up to 6f is a question, but Moore's positioning from a prominent draw will be key.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but that was 44 days ago, and he has fitness to prove on this return; has run over today's trip and going, though ranked 11th of 18 in the field, and 130 lb is no easy burden.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners the in-form Innichen who has won two of his last three starts, both over Goodwood's straight courses; his prominent style and strong course record make him one of the most naturally suited horses to this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Innichen has won his last two starts and finished second three starts back, though he was sixth four starts back — a profile of clear improvement but questions remain over whether he can reproduce that form off 129 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's juvenile has a 6f Goodwood win to his name and has been running consistently if not spectacularly; the 20-day turnaround is short but the trainer has a good recent strike rate and he should be prominent early.
runners_data.comment: Super Tuscan won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving here fresh on a 20-day break with our rating putting him 12lb ahead of his official mark — the main risk is recapturing that winning form after two below-par efforts since.

runners_data.name: Paper View
runners_data.note: Hannon's lightly-weighted juvenile has won twice over course and distance, making his form credentials here strong; naturally a prominent racer by inclination, he is unlikely to get to the front of this large and well-populated field early, which blunts his effectiveness in the most likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Paper View arrives in cracking nick with back-to-back wins, but just four days between races is a quick turnaround, and he ranks ninth of eighteen on our ratings despite carrying 126 lb from stall five; has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's juvenile carries a notable warning having faded late on his two most recent starts at this track; the hold-up style only works if the pace is genuine, and the fade flag makes him difficult to trust even if conditions are otherwise suitable.
runners_data.comment: Wild Terrain won three starts back but has been unplaced in both outings since, and 44 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 89 gives him something to work with.

runners_data.name: May Bee In Profit
runners_data.note: Easterby's juvenile won at 5f on Good to Firm at Goodwood last time and is clearly progressive; she races naturally up with the pace but is pushed back to midfield on the map given the traffic, and Sean Kirrane's inexperience at this level in a field of 18 adds complication to getting a good early position.
runners_data.comment: May Bee In Profit showed a win last time out but has been inconsistent in recent starts — a third and second before that sandwiched a poor ninth — and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, she faces a stiff task after 63 days off, though she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Arabica Queen
runners_data.note: Portman's consistent filly has course and distance form including a 6f Goodwood win; instinctively a prominent racer but with the field loaded with similar types, Rob Hornby will need to be sharp from the gates — she ran just 11 days ago which could be either a freshness positive or a slight fatigue concern.
runners_data.comment: Arabica Queen arrives here in decent nick after a win two starts back, and has run over today's trip, but ranked 14th of 18 on our figures she faces a stiff task; third last time out at least suggests some consistency.

runners_data.name: Social Spirit
runners_data.note: Ray Dawson partners this Michael & David Easterby juvenile whose recent form has deteriorated from a placing to an eighth over 6f at Goodwood last time; the hold-up style in a non-pressing pace looks a tough ask for a horse out of form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 15th of 18 on our figures, Social Spirit has little recent form to recommend him, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 20-day break from stall 18 carrying 120 lb.

runners_data.name: Perigord Noir
runners_data.note: George Baker's juvenile has placed three times without winning and wears headgear; J.F. Egan is a capable booking and the 49-day break gives him time to have freshened up, though the unknown style and lack of a win makes this a speculative runner in a competitive nursery.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — the best he's managed is third three starts back — Perigord Noir is also ranked 17 of 18 on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going. A 49-day absence adds another query.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Tango
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan winless over 14 days going into this and Saffie Osborne's 5lb claim on a hold-up type who has shown very little in two Goodwood starts; after 62 days off the 5f form on soft may not transfer directly to 6f Good to Firm.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a trainer yet to strike in 21 recent attempts, Moonlight Tango is hard to fancy despite her win two starts back; she has experience over today's trip and going, but an eighth last time out and 62 days off the track make her a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Global Success
runners_data.note: J.S. Moore's 2yo has been placed twice at 6f on this course on similar going and is clearly at home at Goodwood; naturally wants to be prominent but will be shuffled back in the pack by the sheer volume of pace-orientated horses, which makes Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim less potent than it would be in a smaller field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a sixth and fifth in there dampening the placings, Global Success is hard to fancy ranked 13 of 18 on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and at least shaped with some promise last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Jaijai is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-horse field over Goodwood's straight six, and with no genuine rival disputing the lead he can dictate a controlled, even gallop on Good to Firm ground — conditions he has handled on all four course visits. Behind him, Sky Secret, Revels, Clash Of Hearts, Dubai Champion, Innichen, and Super Tuscan all want to race prominently, creating a congested chasing pack rather than a pressure cooker, and the pace is therefore likely to be sustainable rather than truly searching. The field contains substantially more prominent-minded types than the race can accommodate in the front ranks; Paper View, May Bee In Profit, Arabica Queen, and Global Success are all genuine prominent racers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all secure their natural position in a field this deep, and it is Sky Secret, Clash Of Hearts, and Innichen — all with course-winning experience — who look best-placed to actually land in the prominent seats. A controlled pace set by Jaijai with a bunched prominent group just behind him means the race is most likely to be decided by those racing in the first half of the field, making the prominent/front-end profile the dominant tactical advantage, with hold-up horses likely to find this unfolding too slowly at the front for a late run to materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaijai Controls, Nearest Win
scenarios.trigger: If Jaijai bowls along at a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent chasers settle just off his heels, allowing the race to be run to suit those tracking from close range.
scenarios.body: Jaijai sets a rhythm that suits horses immediately behind him, and the Good to Firm surface rewards those who travel smoothly in the first three or four — the race becomes a sprint for home from two furlongs out with the winner likely to emerge from the chasing group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group produces a genuine pace duel as several horses push to take second position, injecting enough pace to set up a test of stamina.
scenarios.body: The heightened early tempo burns off the less resolute front-runners and suits horses with a strong finishing effort who were always travelling just off the pace; a horse that settles beautifully in third or fourth and possesses course form is ideally placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the first three furlongs to open up a gap that allows a closer to make sustained ground through the field.
scenarios.body: Persian Spring, the most proven hold-up type with a Goodwood win on similar going, would be best positioned to benefit from any late gap, and Wild Terrain could also factor if the pace is strong enough to spread the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If runners drawn wide struggle to cross, causing traffic problems that reshuffle the order and fragment the field mid-race, allowing an opportunist to slip through.
scenarios.body: The sheer size of the field over Goodwood's six furlongs increases the chance of positional interference in the early stages, and a horse with a versatile style like The Dancing Pirate — shown as unknown style with course form — could capitalise on the disorder.

watchPoints.text: Jaijai (Pat Dobbs) has a clear lead over the entire field as the only natural front-runner — if he bowls clear uncontested on Good to Firm he could prove very hard to reel in, particularly with Hannon's strong current form (11/52 in 14 days).

With at least five genuine prominent types (Sky Secret, Clash Of Hearts, Innichen, Dubai Champion, Super Tuscan) all bidding for the same ground just behind Jaijai, watch for a positional scramble in the first two furlongs that could cause interference and dramatically affect the race outcome.

Paper View, May Bee In Profit, Arabica Queen, and Global Success are all natural front-end horses who will be squeezed back by the sheer volume of prominent rivals — if any of them get boxed in mid-pack on a day when the pace is not pressuring enough, their chance is effectively gone.

Wild Terrain's repeated late fades at this course (positions 21, 12 across his last two Goodwood starts) make him a significant each-way risk despite Hugo Palmer's course knowledge — monitor closely in-running for the same pattern.

Persian Spring is the only proven hold-up horse with a genuine course win on similar going; Jamie Spencer's waiting tactics only pay off if the pace through the first three furlongs is strong — in a Jaijai-controlled scenario this race may simply not set up for a closer.

races.name: World Pool Bet With The Tote Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Silver State
runners_data.note: The pace-controlling asset in this race, she set a comfortable lead last time at Southwell (49 days ago) and her visor sharpens her; at OR 90 she carries top weight and Rose Dawes' 5lb claim helps, but her style fit score flags she may be racing out of her most comfortable prominent role — the front is likely her by default here, not necessarily where she thrives most.
runners_data.comment: Silver State has been placed in two of his last two starts and, as the top-rated runner in the field, he arrives with solid recent form and experience over today's distance and going — the main concern is whether 49 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Won over 10f at Goodwood and showed solid Goodwood course form; Richard Hannon's yard is in good 14-day form and Joe Leavy gets a prominent position that suits this horse perfectly — seven runs on similar going without a win on that surface is a mild caution.
runners_data.comment: Pearl River boasts a win and a runner-up finish in his recent starts, and with experience over today's trip and conditions, he arrives fit on a 20-day break. The main risk is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Echo Of Stars
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes over on this Oliver Cole-trained filly who won over 10f at Goodwood and has placed twice on this course; she is a genuine hold-up type and Spencer will time his run, though the moderate pace scenario is the enemy of her style.
runners_data.comment: Echo Of Stars won two starts back but has been unplaced on his most recent outing, and 41 days off the track adds a fitness query. He has run over today's trip and going, and carries 133 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Pierian
runners_data.note: William Haggas's progressive 3yo has won twice on Good at Goodwood and placed in all four career starts — Tom Marquand keeps the ride and this horse's course and distance profile over 12f here is the standout stat; handles the step to 1m3f on proven form.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in her latest start after back-to-back wins, Pierian hasn't run in 43 days and our rating ranks her twelfth of fourteen — hard to fancy on these figures, though she has run over today's trip and going before, and her recent sequence shows she can win.

runners_data.name: Into The Light
runners_data.note: William Buick and Charlie Appleby send out a horse who placed twice over 12f at Goodwood in good company, but his Goodwood return over this trip last time was a disappointing eleventh — the prominent headgear flag and 0W1P on similar going tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Into The Light showed consistency with two seconds and a win in his last four starts, but returns after 43 days off and an unplaced effort latest — he has experience over today's trip and going, though, and a rating of 92 gives him claims from stall two.

runners_data.name: Waterford Castle
runners_data.note: A remarkably consistent horse with five placings from nine similar-going runs but no win — George Boughey's 3yo trails the field in hold-up fashion (Billy Loughnane up) and needs the race to develop into a stamina test rather than a sprint from a moderate tempo.
runners_data.comment: Waterford Castle has been a model of consistency, finishing second five times in his last six starts — the main concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and may find it hard to break that duck now.

runners_data.name: Steel Raven
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's lightly-raced 3yo won his last start over 10f at Goodwood and has shown a consistent prominent style — only three career runs means he is still unexposed, and stepping to 1m3f for the first time is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Steel Raven won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but carrying 131 lb from stall 13 and rated four pounds below his official mark, he faces a stiff ask to back it up.

runners_data.name: Leonardo Blu
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's horse has won once and placed twice from three starts all over 8f at Goodwood — the step to 1m3f today is a significant trip test for a horse with no evidence of staying this far and David Egan's booking is an interesting signal.
runners_data.comment: Leonardo Blu won two starts back but has since finished fourth, and with our rating of 77 ranking him 11th of 14 runners, he looks up against it here despite going experience and a return after 18 days suggesting he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Devil's Peak
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's hold-up performer won over 11f at Goodwood 14 days ago, is clearly in form, and James Doyle takes over — the blinkers are noted and his in-running profile suits a true-run race but the moderate pace scenario partially undermines him.
runners_data.comment:
Devil's Peak won last time out and arrives here just 14 days later in peak freshness, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour. Carrying 127 lb from stall 10, he rates higher than his official mark of 82 suggests and looks the one to side with.
